name: The Marble Court
summary: A stone hotel behind a working portico, one street up from the river.
description: The Marble Court sits behind a nineteenth-century portico in Chiado, a short walk uphill from the Tagus. Twenty-two rooms open onto a quiet internal courtyard, where breakfast is served under the orange trees from 07:30.

Rooms keep to stone, oak and linen: blackout curtains, a proper desk, rain showers and windows that open. The rooftop terrace looks across the Baixa roofs to the castle, and the bar downstairs pours Portuguese wine by the glass until midnight.
Tram 28 stops at the corner, Baixa-Chiado metro is a four-minute walk, and the river walk starts two streets away.

name: The Lantern House
summary: A tall stone townhouse below the Galata Tower, with a roof that looks across the Golden Horn.
description: The Lantern House fills a narrow 1890s apartment building on Serdar-ı Ekrem, the steep lane that runs down from the Galata Tower. Sixteen rooms climb six floors, each with tall windows, plaster ceilings and copper lamps made in the Grand Bazaar.

Breakfast is laid out on the roof from 07:00: simit, white cheese, olives, tomatoes and tea in tulip glasses. In the evening the same roof turns into a small bar with a view over the Golden Horn to the mosques of the old city.
Karaköy, the ferries and the tram are all downhill. İstiklal Avenue is five minutes up the other way.

summary: A Belle Époque beach resort on the Lido, with a private beach and a boat to St Mark's.
description: The Lido Gardens is a restored 1908 seaside hotel facing the Adriatic, with its own stretch of beach and striped cabanas. Gardens of pine and oleander separate it from the road.
A private launch crosses the lagoon to St Mark's in fifteen minutes, so you can spend the morning on the beach and the evening in the city.

description: This bright one-bedroom apartment takes the whole top floor of a neoclassical house on Kydathineon, the pedestrian street through Plaka. Steps lead up to a private roof terrace with a table, two loungers and the Acropolis straight ahead.
The kitchen is fully equipped, and the host leaves Greek coffee, honey and fruit for your first morning.

There is a proper desk, fast WiFi and a kitchen for simple meals. The Marché des Enfants Rouges is three minutes away.

summary: A two-bedroom loft above a wine bar in Monti, ten minutes' walk from the Colosseum.
description: A converted workshop on Via Panisperna, with a mezzanine bedroom, a second bedroom below and a long kitchen table for six. Brick vaults and big steel windows keep it cool in summer.
Monti's piazza, with its fountain and evening crowd, is two minutes down the hill. The Colosseum is ten minutes away on foot.

description: A bright two-bedroom flat in an old bonded warehouse on The Shore, the cobbled quay where the Water of Leith meets the harbour. The living room looks straight over the water.
Some of Edinburgh's best seafood restaurants are downstairs, and the tram takes you to Princes Street in twenty minutes.

summary: A wooden waterside mansion on the Asian shore, with its own jetty on the Bosphorus.
description: A restored nineteenth-century yalı in Kuzguncuk, painted oxblood red and standing right on the water. Four bedrooms, a long salon and a waterside terrace with its own jetty.
A housekeeper prepares breakfast every morning, and a private boat can take you across to the old city in twenty minutes.

Rosa, the cook, will make breakfast or a full Oaxacan dinner on request. The centre is fifteen minutes away by car or taxi.

description: Villa Pergola sits on the hillside at Pogerola, three hundred metres above Amalfi. A long pergola of vines and lemons shades the terrace, and an infinity pool looks straight down the coast.
Four bedrooms each have their own bathroom. A cook and a driver can be arranged, and the bus to Amalfi stops at the gate.

name: Casa da Foz
summary: A tiled family house where the Douro meets the Atlantic, with a garden and a tram to the city.
description: Casa da Foz is a 1920s house faced in blue and white azulejos, on the promenade where the Douro river meets the sea. Three bedrooms, a sunny garden with a lemon tree and a fireplace for Atlantic evenings.
The historic tram 1 runs along the river to Ribeira in twenty minutes, and the beaches of Foz are across the road.
